paper_metadata.title: Applying the Quantum Grover Algorithm to Improve the Efﬁciency of Growth Models

summary: The paper proposes using Grover’s quantum search algorithm to accelerate parameter optimization in the Solow and Cobb‑Douglas economic growth models. It argues theoretically that parameter search complexity could be reduced from O(N) classical search to O(sqrt(N)) using Grover’s algorithm, but provides no numerical experiments, circuit implementations, or benchmark results.

experiments.description: Grover-based optimization of parameters in economic growth models (Solow and Cobb-Douglas) to search for stable stationary states and improve parameter-finding efficiency.

algorithm.variant: Grover search for optimal parameters in growth models

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Search over an unordered set of candidate parameter values; the paper describes a binary oracle f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} and Grover search over input registers, but does not specify a concrete qubit-to-variable mapping for the economic parameters.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find parameter values that optimize/stabilize the Solow and Cobb-Douglas growth models; the paper frames this as searching for x0 such that f(x0)=1, where f encodes the desired property of the model parameters/stationary state.

problem_instance.description: Economic growth-model parameter optimization for the Solow model and Cobb-Douglas model; stability of steady states is analyzed.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical derivation plus conceptual quantum-algorithm description; no numerical benchmark protocol, repeated runs, or dataset split reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical derivation of the Solow and Cobb-Douglas differential equations and steady-state conditions; Grover is presented as a faster search method for parameter selection.

results.unit: candidate parameter values in the example lists

speedup_claims.conditions: for unstructured search over an unordered database of size N
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents Grover’s algorithm conceptually and does not report an implemented gate-based experiment, hardware run, or measured runtime.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical search over an unordered database
speedup_claims.conditions: for Grover search on an unordered database of n elements
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the asymptotic advantage as sqrt(n) operations versus classical n/2 on average and n-1 in the worst case; no empirical benchmark or hardware experiment is reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: reported in the results/discussion for parameter search in the Solow and Cobb-Douglas models
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a benchmark protocol, raw timing data, or run counts; the claim is stated qualitatively.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical exhaustive search over candidate parameters
speedup_claims.conditions: stated for Grover search over an unordered set of candidate parameter values; no hardware experiment reported
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper gives a conceptual Grover-based parameter search description and states O(sqrt(N)) versus O(N) classical search, but does not report an implemented gate-based benchmark, qubit count, or measured runtime.
